messages.subject: Implementation of Congdon (2017)
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to implement in Nimble the model proposed by Congdon (2017) for spatial effects. I have fitted it in Stan but would like to check that I am doing the right thing by using another software and comparing the results.. Enters Nimble. Assuming a 0-1 neighbourhood matrix, the conditional distributions are defined as follows:

s_i | s_{-i} ~ N(lambda/[1-lambda + lambda*d_i] * sum_{j ~ i} kappa_j*s_j ; sigma^2/[kappa_i*(1-lambda+lambda*d_i)]),

where d_i is the ith area's number of neighbours. The vector of N kappa's are additional latent effects.

I wonder if anyone here has managed to run this model in Nimble?

For reference, I have tried to implement it with the conditional distributions, which yield a cyclic graph and returns an error because of that. I saw on this group that CAR models need to be specified through their joint distributions to avoid this error. However, in this case, the joint distribution is a normal with mean 0 and precision matrix 1/sigma^2 * diag(kappa_i)*[(1-lambda)*I + lambda*(D-W_tilde)], where W_tilde = [w_{ij}*kappa_j] and D=diag(d_i). This precision matrix is not necessarily proper and this causes Nimble to not work.

Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Best,
Victoire

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Implementation of Congdon (2017)
parts:
Hi Victoire,

I'm sorry about the delay in responding. Your message ended up in my spam folder (and the same might have happened for others on the Nimble team).

Indeed, the CAR model needs to be specified jointly to avoid the cyclic graph. We have the `dcar_normal` distribution precisely for this purpose. Have you tried using that? We have a chapter on CAR models in our manual. If you have already seen that, please give us more details on why it won't work in your case.

Also you may know of this, but here is a recent manuscript providing a more efficient way to use CAR models in Stan: https://osf.io/3ey65/.

-chris
